# Factory Launch, Iterations, and Health

FactoryLauncher owns setup/resumption and external operating conditions;
Factory owns production after accepting the handoff. Use this procedure with
[Factory MVP and Recovery](../SKILL.md), not as additional authority.

## Select the assignment mode

| Mode | Work and exit |
| --- | --- |
| New Factory | Investigate existing identity/product records, establish the bounded mandate and prerequisites, hand control to Factory, and verify the first demonstrated value increment. |
| Resume | Reconcile existing records, authority, partial work and runtime; restore already-authorized production without replacing the product or repeating answered setup questions. |
| Discovery only | Accept and hand off bounded VOC research with permissions, deliverable and exit criteria. Do not require delivery readiness or iterations 1-10 before this handoff, mobilize delivery, or claim setup MVP. |
| Health only | Inspect the agreed operating conditions, perform permitted recovery and return evidence and the next checkpoint. Do not restart the interview, invoke Factory again or take production control. |
| Queue-exhaustion validation | Independently validate the common closure snapshot under the shared recovery contract. Return the verdict and invoker-sign-off packet; do not interview, mobilize delivery or invoke Factory. |

An explicit human setup/resume request authorizes its recorded bounded mission
and routine internal delegation, not new scope, unapproved spending, external
contact/private access, deployment or release. Future iterations retain their
own authorization. Do not ask again for authority already supplied.

Bind the accepted [operating profile](../SKILL.md#operating-profiles) before
depending on its capabilities. New engagements propose bounded operation;
existing terms are not silently migrated. A bounded checkpoint returns evidence
and a real resume route, not Factory closure or setup MVP without a verified
first value increment.

Distinguish the human owner, Factory, product owner and product workspace.
For an agentic product, identify its runtime agents and architecture separately
from ADHD development agents. Investigate an existing Factory/product before
creating either; preserve identity, history and unfinished work.

## Interview and evidence collection

1. Read applicable repository instructions and existing canonical records.
   Retrieve product storage guidance before writing. Extract confirmed facts,
   sources, conflicts and missing decisions before questioning the invoker.
2. Establish decision rights, source/access/consent boundaries and the shared
   session tool grant. Reuse live grants and keep authentication human-only.
3. Ask one focused question for the highest-impact missing authorization or
   card-enrichment input after safe analysis within the mandate is exhausted.
   For an impasse, provide a recommended Yes/No decision, its exact action,
   consequences and alternatives. Route questions through the parent when a
   delegate cannot ask.
4. Record sanitized decision IDs, answer/source/time, approver and authority,
   status, affected record, unresolved issue, owner and next action. Link the
   canonical contract instead of duplicating authority or private content.
5. Reassess readiness after material answers. Label each criterion confirmed,
   evidenced not applicable, or unresolved. Unknowns may become authorized
   discovery with measurable exits, not a waiver of delivery or safety gates.
6. Complete required setup and first-cycle work before optional efficiency
   analysis. Do not introduce routine finish/continue/pause menus, repeat
   answered questions, or let optional detail become a new approval gate.

Missing numeric operating terms follow the shared empirical-baseline procedure.
Measured proposals remain provisional until confirmed and grant no authority.

## Readiness evidence

Use one matrix with criterion, source/revision, accountable owner, observed
result/status, gap and next action. All applicable mandatory criteria must pass.

| Criterion | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Identity and purpose | Existing/new identity, human owner and escalation route; beneficiaries, user/operational job, non-users, anti-goals, foreseeable harm and binding ethical/legal/privacy/security constraints. |
| Mandate | Approved assignment mode and operating profile, scope/exclusions, decision rights, operating and iteration horizons, resources/budget, checkpoints/resume owner, consequential approvals and revocation route. |
| Value | Baseline or authorized measurement, smallest cumulative increment, outcome measure, threshold, counterevidence and review rule. Intent is not verified benefit. |
| Records | Product-owned repository/workspace and guidance; canonical index/contract, designated writers, privacy-safe Git evidence and compatible existing paths. |
| Roster and runtime | Actual accepted role assignments and callable tools for the selected profile. Bounded work invokes accountable roles as needed; parallel/supervised work requires VOC, ProductOwner, chief-chartered AssociateProductOwner, Kanban and Squad/Fullstacker with observed overlap. Default one Squad of three unless an approved exception applies. |
| Flow | Authoritative backlog/board, approved WIP/reserve units and limits, eligible True Ready IDs/evidence, priority, readiness-assignment authority, lead time/triggers and completion destination. |
| Continuity | Current/next accepted assignments, permitted fallback exits, deadlines, resource/authority renewal, health custody and executor, recovery panel and real restart route. |
| Technical gates | Applicable acceptance/Definition of Done, architecture/security/testability, completed prerequisites, independent bounded scope, environment access, validation and integration owner. |
| Observation and history | Product-owned Operations Center readiness/capture gaps and accepted Historian assignment for mandatory demand intake/events. Full transcript capture remains separately scoped; no every-turn listener is implied. |
| Iterations and learning | The rolling plan below, cumulative demo/feedback and next-authorization checkpoints, post-10 cadence and iteration-36 calibration. |
| Product placement | Starting reference/version, layout and invocation guidance, distinct runtime-agent identity, approved deviations and `src/` fallback when the reference is silent. |
| Setup MVP/resumption | Observed acceptance and mobilization, then demonstrated, empirically verified first value increment for setup or restored authorized value-producing progress for resume. |

A delivery claim additionally needs the first card's current True Ready
evidence and WIP admission from Kanban and technical evidence from delivery.
Discovery-only work cannot inherit implementation authority. A missing
investment policy blocks new financial approval, not already-authorized bounded
analysis. A prepared package, template or intended roster is not setup MVP.
If a hard runtime/permission limit prevents activation, report the exact failed
criterion, conditional next action and restart route instead of claiming success.

## Iteration and cadence contract

Make iteration 1 executable before delivery activation. Keep iterations 2-10
as explicit provisional themes, dependencies, uncertainty and refinement
checkpoints; do not invent detailed answers or future results. Their unknown
detail must not block the authorized first cycle.

For each currently authorized iteration, establish:

- Customer/operational outcome, smallest cumulative increment and rationale.
- Applicable dissatisfiers, including harm, reliability, usability, performance,
  security, privacy, accessibility, support and business-model failure modes.
- Satisfiers and predeclared observable acceptance measures.
- Definition of Done, inherited gates, acceptable not-applicable rationale,
  verification method and separate release decision.
- Dependencies, assumptions, risks, permissions, budget/timebox/burn,
  accountable roster, capacity and required skills.
- Cumulative demo audience, environment, scenario, presenter, date/cadence,
  accessibility, evidence and feedback-capture method.
- Feedback rules for retaining, enriching, pruning, reordering, splitting,
  retiring or overlaying product direction and artifacts.
- Authorization owner and evidence to start, verify Done Done, demo and
  authorize the next iteration.

At each boundary:

1. Obtain integrated, criterion-by-criterion Done Done evidence; keep residuals
   on the unfinished board. Demo all retained prior increments plus the new
   increment against approved scenarios.
2. Record actual audience/environment, observations, failures, questions,
   feedback, dissent and unavailable evidence. Route evidence to VOC and
   product/economic decisions to ProductOwner.
3. Have accountable owners reconcile the charter, evidence, backlog, economics,
   plan, architecture, acceptance/DoD, roster and operating records. Kanban
   represents each unfinished item once.
4. An evidence-supported overlay preserves the replaced baseline and history,
   maps retained/replaced/retired work, evaluates migration/recovery and obtains
   any required mandate/investment/safety/release approvals.
5. Reforecast the remaining horizon and refine the next iteration from results.
   Reassess scale from demand, readiness, dependencies, bottlenecks, quality,
   runtime and incremental burn. Dedicated subproduct splits retain the
   associate scaling gate and ProductOwner agreement.
6. Obtain next-iteration authorization after its scope, measures, demo/feedback,
   roster, skills, budget and permissions reflect the latest evidence.

Before iteration 1, record cadence and the decision route. Before the initial
10-iteration horizon ends, obtain the invoker's continuation/cadence decision;
repeat before later horizons expire. Cadence is not a pause instruction.
Complete VOC, Kanban and empirical-product calibration before iteration 37:
reconcile evidence/counterevidence, accepted/rejected hypotheses, unfinished and
completed work, demos/outcomes, quality/harm, actual versus forecast economics,
product behavior and retained/pruned/overlaid artifacts. Preserve contradictions,
owner decisions and the calibrated baseline. Missing calibration blocks
authorization past the gate, not unaffected authorized work.

## Artifact placement and handoff

Follow the product's established formats and storage guidance; use
`.docs/factories/<safe-name>/` only when compatible. Validate safe names and
workspace confinement. Resolve conflicting legacy paths through an authorized
compatibility/migration decision, not duplicate authorities.

Documented records and invocable products have different placement rules.
Follow the product-development reference's versioned layout/invocation guidance.
When silent, put executable product source in an approved product-specific
`src/` directory, not `.docs/`. Record deviations, authority, migration impact
and validation; copied examples do not prove best practice.

Maintain these logical records as existing sections/references where possible,
not a requirement to create a file per row:

| Record | Contents and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Manifest/charter/index | Identity, purpose, beneficiaries, mode, scope/exclusions, value hypothesis, limits and authoritative record locators; Launcher consolidates approved decisions. |
| Authority/engagement | Decision provenance, permitted/prohibited actions, scope/validity/expiry, revocation/renewal, acceptance, writers and consequential checkpoints; canonical contract schema applies. |
| Evidence/demand | Source-linked observations/hypotheses, counterevidence, consent/access, limitations and next validation; VOC owns custody and analysis. |
| Backlog/economics | Stable IDs, outcomes/dispositions/order, criteria, dependencies, compatible costs/benefits, policy status and review terms; ProductOwner owns decisions. |
| Board/completion/gates | Kanban's complete two-bucket inventory, readiness/WIP evidence, completion destination and gate/DoD evidence; delivery supplies technical proof. |
| Iteration/demo/adaptation | Planned versus actual cumulative demos, feedback, decisions, retained/pruned/overlaid work, cadence and calibration; accountable owners supply evidence. |
| Operating/cycle/health | Accepted production/readiness custody, actual executor, resources/authority, current/next assignments, reserves, fallback, deadlines, outcomes, burn, recovery and next checkpoint. |
| Product references | Every invocable product's starting reference/version, workspace/layout, invocation surface, runtime agents, deviations and verification. |
| Roster/handoffs | Requested versus observed instances, accepted boundaries, interface/integration ownership, permitted concurrency, shared-write serialization and scale/rollback evidence. |
| Closure/escalation | Common closure snapshot, source reconciliation, role attestations, Launcher verdict, discrepancies, risks/reopen terms, costed recovery decisions, invoker sign-off and restart route. |

Handoffs identify the approved revision, mode/authority, memory binding,
applicable evidence, bounded assignments, accepted receivers and first safe
action. Give one-shot delegates their complete assignment and predeclared
acceptance-event protocol; do not depend on a later activation message.
Validate saved coverage, links, identity, approvals, limits, Git state and
specialist evidence before claiming readiness.

## Operating readiness and health

1. Agree cadence/triggers, warning thresholds, evidence freshness, renewal lead
   time and actual execution owner. Check on handoff, agreed checkpoints,
   material change, forecast expiry and reported extrinsic impediments.
2. Revalidate source authority, live host grant, scope, expiry/revocation and
   remaining budget/horizon. Never silently renew or extend authorizations.
   Expired, revoked, stale, or out-of-scope authority blocks affected actions;
   continue unaffected authorized work.
3. Inspect dated progress, accepted current/next assignments, roster/resources,
   remaining capacity/burn, reserve forecasts and dependencies. Missing/stale
   evidence is unverified health.
4. Leave intrinsic flow to Factory. For extrinsic risks record impact, onset,
   owner, authorized recovery, deadline and success evidence; obtain the
   smallest missing owner decision early.
5. Hand accepted recovery to Factory and verify restored conditions and
   progress. Preserve failed attempts, open risks and the next check.
6. Before the window/runtime ends, secure accepted custody or an honest resume
   route. The procedure does not install a scheduler. Continuing checks need a
   separately authorized, verified host/supervisor or human executor.

## Optional improvement topics

After required setup, consider only mission-relevant learning quality,
economics, flow/capacity, engineering integration, operational readiness,
benefit/harm distribution and feedback quality. For each proposal state its
mechanism, cost/tradeoff, uncertainty, measure and owner decision. Optional
analysis cannot delay setup MVP or become a hidden gate.
